401	/** SIGKILL grace after the SIGTERM on abort/timeout — gives the child a moment
402	 *  to flush + exit cleanly before we hard-kill. */
403	const KILL_GRACE_MS = 2_000;
404	
405	/** The raw subprocess spawn + timeout-kill + stdout/stderr capture (never rejects). */
406	function runChild(
407	  command: string,
408	  args: string[],
409	  projectDir: string,
410	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
411	  role: string,
412	  signal?: AbortSignal,
413	  timeoutMs?: number,
414	  onChildPid?: (pid: number) => void,
415	  onOutputActivity?: () => void,
416	): Promise<{ output: string; exitCode: number; stderr: string; timedOut?: boolean }> {
417	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
418	    // Already-aborted before we spawn → don't launch at all.
419	    if (signal?.aborted) {
420	      resolve({ output: '', exitCode: 1, stderr: 'aborted before start' });
421	      return;
422	    }
423	    let timedOut = false;
424	    // `detached: true` puts the child in its OWN process group so we can reap the
425	    // WHOLE tree on abort/timeout, not just the immediate child. In dev the spawn is
426	    // `node <tsx-cli> invoke-once.ts`, and the tsx CLI forks a worker (invoke-once,
427	    // which spawns the agent) — a single-PID kill hits only the wrapper and orphans
428	    // the agent (EI-40). Group-kill (`process.kill(-pid)`) takes out wrapper +
429	    // invoke-once + agent together. The new group is the child's alone, so it can
430	    // never signal the operator host (a different group).
431	    const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd: projectDir, env, detached: true });
432	    // EI-85: surface the child OS pid so the caller can record it on the nursery
433	    // row — the reclaim sweep liveness-checks /proc/<pid> rather than blindly
434	    // reclaiming a stale-heartbeat row whose child is actually still alive.
435	    if (child.pid != null) {
436	      try { onChildPid?.(child.pid); } catch { /* recording is best-effort */ }
437	    }
438	    let stdout = '';
439	    let stderr = '';
440	    let killGrace: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
441	    let aborted = false;
442	    // Kill the child's whole process group; fall back to a single-PID kill if the
443	    // group send fails (e.g. the child already exited / no group).
444	    const killTree = (sigName: NodeJS.Signals) => {
445	      const pid = child.pid;
446	      if (pid) { try { process.kill(-pid, sigName); return; } catch { /* fall through */ } }
447	      try { child.kill(sigName); } catch { /* ignore */ }
448	    };
449	    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
450	      timedOut = true;
451	      killTree('SIGTERM');
452	    }, timeoutMs ?? invokeTimeoutMs());
453	    // Caller-driven abort (EI-40: fleet:cancel of an operator spawn): SIGTERM the
454	    // tree now, SIGKILL it after a grace period if it ignores the term.
455	    const onAbort = () => {
456	      aborted = true;
457	      killTree('SIGTERM');
458	      killGrace = setTimeout(() => { killTree('SIGKILL'); }, KILL_GRACE_MS);
459	    };
460	    if (signal) signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
461	    const cleanup = () => {
462	      clearTimeout(timer);
463	      if (killGrace) clearTimeout(killGrace);
464	      if (signal) signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
465	    };
466	    // P-008: every emitted chunk is the mid-turn signal — stderr counts too
467	    // (some backends log progress there while stdout buffers).
468	    const reportActivity = () => { try { onOutputActivity?.(); } catch { /* best-effort */ } };
469	    child.stdout?.on('data', (d) => { reportActivity(); stdout += String(d); });
470	    child.stderr?.on('data', (d) => { reportActivity(); stderr += String(d); });
471	    child.on('close', (code) => {
472	      cleanup();
473	      // A child we aborted may exit 0 (it caught SIGTERM and shut down) or via the
474	      // signal — normalize to a non-zero "aborted" outcome so callers don't read a
475	      // cancelled run as a clean success.
476	      if (aborted) {
477	        resolve({ output: extractAgentOutput(stdout), exitCode: 1, stderr: stderr.trim() || 'aborted (fleet:cancel)' });
478	        return;
479	      }
480	      const exitCode = code ?? 1;
481	      const failLog = formatInvokeStderr(role, exitCode, stderr);
482	      if (failLog) console.error(failLog);
483	      // A non-zero exit with EMPTY stderr is otherwise completely silent (the
484	      // upstream "exit=1 empty=true" hides whether the agent even produced output).
485	      else if (exitCode !== 0) {
486	        const dbg =
487	          process.env.PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_DEBUG === '1'
488	            ? `\n--- stdout tail (${role}) ---\n${stdout.length > 2000 ? stdout.slice(-2000) : stdout}`
489	            : '';
490	        console.error(`[dbos-invoke] role=${role} exited ${exitCode} with empty stderr (stdout ${stdout.length} chars)${dbg}`);
491	      } else if (stderr.trim()) {
492	        // Exit 0 with non-empty stderr: surface it so the operator log shows why
493	        // the bee vanished (e.g. "You've hit your session limit"). Without this,
494	        // exit-0 runs are completely silent even when the stderr carries the cause.
495	        const stderrHead = stderr.trim().slice(0, 500);
496	        console.warn(`[dbos-invoke] role=${role} exited 0 with stderr (${stderr.length} chars): ${stderrHead}`);
497	      }
498	      resolve({ output: extractAgentOutput(stdout), exitCode, stderr, timedOut });
499	    });
500	    child.on('error', (err) => {
501	      cleanup();
502	      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
503	      console.error(`[dbos-invoke] role=${role} spawn error: ${msg}`);
504	      resolve({ output: '', exitCode: 1, stderr: msg });
505	    });
506	  });
507	}
